headline: High: OpenHands can write and execute in a runtime while Khoj can read indexed notes, creating default-path data leakage and output-driven cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj ingests indexed documents and personal notes, while OpenHands can write files and use MCP/browser/tooling inside its runtime. If OpenHands content is copied into Khoj’s indexed corpus or shared files, malicious instructions could be surfaced to Khoj as trusted text. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible.
conditions: IF OpenHands writes attacker-controlled text into a file that Khoj later indexes
IF the two agents share a mounted workspace or copied notes without provenance labels
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Disable automatic indexing of files written by OpenHands
Add a manual review step before Khoj ingests new content
Tag OpenHands-generated files as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj reads personal notes and indexed documents, and OpenHands touches files in its runtime sandbox with broad network egress. If the same workspace or mounted volume is shared, sensitive notes can flow from Khoj-visible files into OpenHands outputs or external calls. This is a default-path risk when users co-locate data, though not proven universal.
conditions: IF both agents access the same mounted directory or copied workspace
IF OpenHands is allowed to transmit file contents to external model providers
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Remove secrets from any shared folder
Restrict OpenHands network access for sensitive runs
Review files before mounting them into OpenHands
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad runtime execution; Khoj has read_filesystem and shared index state across user clients. If both operate on the same files or repository, they can race on mutable artifacts even without explicit coordination. The profiles show overlapping access to shared files, so conflict is plausible in default co-location setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or mounted volume
IF OpenHands modifies files while Khoj indexes or reads them concurrently
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories
Pause indexing during OpenHands edits
Use git branches per agent
Lock the workspace during writes
requires-engineering: add cross-agent file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved notes and documents, and OpenHands can act on files and browser/tool outputs. If OpenHands consumes Khoj’s retrieved text as authoritative, a mistaken or injected retrieval can cascade into edits, commits, or runtime actions. Because OpenHands has action capability and Khoj is a retrieval system, the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses Khoj output as a source of truth without verification
IF retrieved text is converted into shell commands, code changes, or browser actions
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Compare retrieved claims against original sources
Disable auto-acting on retrieved text
Limit OpenHands to read-only mode for Khoj-fed tasks
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is a personal-notes/document system and OpenHands runs files inside a Docker runtime with model-provider API keys. If personal notes include regulated data and are mounted into OpenHands, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across two different processing environments. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated notes are mounted into OpenHands
IF retention or deletion policies differ between Khoj indexing and OpenHands runtime storage
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared mounts
Align retention settings before use
Delete temporary runtime copies after each session
Document where each agent stores data
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware routing
